Description: An attacker submits crafted input directly, or plants instructions in content the chatbot retrieves (indirect injection), to override the chatbot's instructions; the risk arises because the model cannot reliably separate instructions from data and no input or output validation is in place; the chatbot could give members unauthorized or misleading responses, such as false contact details or fraudulent links, resulting in member harm, complaints, and regulatory and reputational exposure. A successful injection may also enable R-04 and R-05. The residual impact score assumes the R-05 treatment is complete.
Planned Controls: Input filtering for direct and indirect injection patterns; output validation before responses are displayed; adversarial testing before launch and before each release

Description: An attacker uses crafted prompts to induce the chatbot to disclose nonpublic personal information (NPI) embedded in knowledge base documents that were not sanitized of member data before ingestion and are returned without output filtering; such disclosure could expose NPI to unauthorized parties and may trigger notification to affected members under the New York SHIELD Act and regulator notification under NYDFS Part 500 and NCUA Part 748 where each rule's threshold is met, and could result in NCUA or NYDFS enforcement action and reputational harm.
Existing Controls: System prompt instructions; vendor default safety filters
Planned Controls: PII scanning and redaction before ingestion; output filtering for NPI patterns; recurring prompt injection testing and knowledge base audits

Description: Through adversarial prompting or unprompted model hallucination, the chatbot may present incorrect loan or deposit rates, fees, hours, or account procedures because this information is drawn from knowledge base documents that are not updated when it changes, documents have no defined review or expiration cycle, and rate responses are not validated against an authoritative rate source; members could make financial decisions based on inaccurate information, exposing Brightwater to member complaints, potential obligations to honor quoted rates, and compliance issues under Truth in Savings (NCUA Part 707) and Truth in Lending (Regulation Z).
Existing Controls: Ad hoc manual removal of outdated documents; system prompt disclaimer
Planned Controls: Retrieve rates from an authoritative read-only rate source instead of knowledge base documents; automatic dated disclaimer on responses containing rates; daily automated testing of rate answers against the authoritative source; document lifecycle metadata with automatic exclusion of expired content

Description: An attacker uses direct requests, encoding or translation techniques, role play, or hypothetical framing to extract the chatbot's system prompt; the risk arises because the prompt contains guardrail logic and internal details and the design relies on its secrecy as a security control; disclosure could enable guardrail bypass and reveal internal business logic.
Existing Controls: System prompt instruction not to reveal its instructions; vendor default safety filters
Planned Controls: Remove internal details from the system prompt; input classifier to detect extraction attempts; automated extraction testing with garak before each release

Description: An attacker or an ordinary member may retrieve internal policy content through chatbot responses because internal policies and member FAQs reside in the same vector database and the database does not inherit the access controls (ACLs) of the source documents; such exposure could reveal sensitive internal procedures, including fraud thresholds and exception handling, aiding fraudulent activity and creating regulatory and reputational exposure.
Existing Controls: System prompt instruction to use only public information
Planned Controls: Remove internal policy documents from the chatbot knowledge base; metadata-based access filtering on vector search as a backup control; allowlist-based ingestion pipeline for approved public content only

Description: A contributor with knowledge base write access, or an attacker using a compromised contributor account, uploads or modifies a document so that it contains false or misleading content; the risk arises because ingestion relies on contributor trust, with no independent content review, change logging, or integrity verification of approved documents; the chatbot could give members manipulated guidance, including falsified contact details that direct members to fraud, resulting in member harm, complaints, and regulatory and reputational exposure. This risk covers false content; instructions planted in documents are covered under R-01.
Existing Controls: Knowledge base write access limited to designated contributors
Planned Controls: Dual approval and change logging before publication; SHA-256 integrity monitoring of source documents and chunks

Risk: Unsafe chatbot output rendered in website or app
Description: An attacker uses prompt injection or tampered knowledge base content to make the chatbot return HTML or script; the risk arises because the website and mobile app render model output as active content without encoding or sanitization, and the chat interface shares an origin with authenticated online banking pages; the content could execute in a member's browser or in the mobile app's embedded web view, leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or redirection to a fraudulent site, with member harm and regulatory and reputational exposure. Fraudulent links shown as text are covered under R-01. Related to R-01 and R-06.
Planned Controls: Context-aware output encoding and HTML sanitization before rendering; chat interface hosted on a separate origin or in a sandboxed frame; links restricted to an allowlist of Brightwater domains; Content Security Policy on the chat interface
